newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends volatile session mainly weaker.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends volatile session mainly weaker.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures ended mostly weaker and toward the middle of the day's wide range on Tuesday, after a rollercoaster session which saw prices run-up to new eight-year highs and fall sharply in the first hour of trading.
Benchmark September ended $4 a tonne lower, at $1,625, after ranging between a new life-of-contract high of $1,655 and $1,598.
Spot July, which entered delivery period today, rose $3, to $1,584, after rallying to a lifetime high of $1,620 -- the highest spot price on a continuous weekly chart since 1989.
The remaining contracts finished $7 to $13 lower.
Cocoa prices rose at the opening, bolstered by fund-led buying. Momentum accelerated after September pierced key resistance levels, touching off a series of buy-stops.
But a round of origin selling and profit-taking halted the rally and pushed September more than $20 lower before local short-covering and light speculative buying trimmed losses, traders said.

"The fund buying in the morning didn't garner any further buying and we had producer selling and profit-taking," one trader said. "Technically, the market was overbought, but there's buying on any dip because there is still a load of bullish sentiment."

Last week, September cocoa surged $177 or about 12 percent on talk of a preliminary estimate for a smaller 1997/98 Ivorian crop and fears that a developing weather pattern called El Nino could bring damaging conditions to key cocoa-growing regions.
Some market participants, however, doubted that the cocoa market could sustain the upswing in the short-term.
"They do have the problem of abundent stocks," said Refco Inc analyst Ann Prendergast. "There is no safeguard against a price rise but unless those stocks are diminished, they are negative."

Prendergast said the longer-term fundamental outlook was more bullish mainly because of El Nino. "The El Nino effect is real," she said. "It's going to be a continuous factor giving fundamental support."

Some traders said the market was still overbought and that September may have to fill a $1,540-$1,516 chart gap formed last Thursday, before the market could make further gains. In the near-term, they said September support was seen near today's low at $1,598.
After Tuesday's close, the CSCE said it will raise margins on all cocoa contracts by $100, to $600, effective June 18.
